How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build the RESTful GET request you’ll need to hit the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** (v6.3.1) to fetch the *Speed* information for a specific interface. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | Base URL | `https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | Query Parameters | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=Ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | --- ### 1. Full URL (with query string) ``` https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` --- ### 2. Example `curl` command ```bash curl -k \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=Ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` > **Tip:** > * `-k` skips certificate verification (use only if you’re sure the cert is trusted). > * Replace `-k` with proper TLS handling in production. --- ### 3. Using the provided `requests_get` function (Python) If you’d like to invoke the request programmatically via the helper function, here’s how: ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", params={ "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } ) print(response) ``` > **Note:** > The function will internally perform the GET request and return the parsed JSON (or raw response) as per its implementation. --- ### 4. What to expect in the response A successful call will return JSON similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "Ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speedMbps": 1000, "timestamp": "2026-10-14T12:34:56Z" } ``` If the interface isn’t found or the parameters are wrong, you’ll receive an error object: ```json { "error": { "code": 404, "message": "Interface not found" } } ``` --- ### 5. Quick checklist - ✅ Verify the IP (`192.120.45.67`) is reachable from your client machine. - ✅ Ensure you have the necessary credentials (basic auth, token, etc.) – add them to the `curl` header or the function call if required. - ✅ Confirm that the API version (`v1`) and endpoint path match your Nexus Dashboard installation. - ✅ Double‑check the parameter values (`fabricName`, `nodeId`, `podId`, `interfaceType`, `infoType`) against your environment. That’s all you need to generate and execute the RESTful request for the “get information of an interface” API on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Happy querying!
